Monsoon to drench Kerala in heavy rain: IMD issues orange alert till August 2
An active southwest monsoon is gathering strength over Kerala, prompting weather alerts across districts. With rain expected to intensify in coming days, authorities are closely monitoring the situation as the risk of disruptions rises in vulnerable regions.

Tourists at the Fort Kochi Beach as dark clouds hover over the skyline, in Ernakulam district, Kerala. (Photo: PTI)
A fresh spell of monsoon rain is set to lash Kerala over the next few days, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecasting heavy rainfall across several parts of the state from Thursday, July 30.
The weather office has issued rain alerts for all districts through August 2, warning that the intensity and spread of rainfall will increase as the monsoon remains active.
For Thursday, the IMD has placed Wayanad, Kozhikode and Kannur under an orange alert, indicating the likelihood of heavy to very heavy rainfall at isolated places.
The remaining districts are also expected to receive widespread showers, with yellow alerts in place for Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Ernakulam, Idukki, Thrissur, Palakkad, Malappuram and Kasaragod.
Wayanad has even directed schools to remain shut as rain intensifies across the region.
With heavy rain expected, authorities declared a holiday for all educational institutions in Wayanad on Thursday as a precautionary measure.
However, the order does not apply to residential schools and colleges, which will function as scheduled unless separate instructions are issued.
The fresh spell of rain comes as the southwest monsoon remains active over Kerala.
During this phase of the monsoon, moisture-laden winds from the Arabian Sea often trigger widespread rainfall across the state, particularly over the northern districts and the Western Ghats, where intense showers are common.
EXTENDED ALERTS ACROSS GOD'S OWN COUNTRY
The weather department has also issued alerts for every district on Friday, July 31, indicating that rainfall is likely to become more widespread across the state.
The exact alert category varies by district and is expected to be updated through regular IMD bulletins based on the evolving weather situation.
Kerala has been witnessing an active southwest monsoon in recent weeks, with recurring spells of heavy rain affecting several districts.
Naturally, with heavier rain spells incoming, the risk of waterlogging in urban areas, rising river levels and disruptions is set to rise, particularly in hilly regions that are prone to landslides during intense rainfall.

Authorities urge water conservation amid third-level heat alert
According to a Wednesday forecast by HungaroMet Zrt., the daily mean temperature on Thursday could exceed 27 degrees Celsius in Northern Transdanubia, the central part of the country, and the Southern Great Plain, prompting the meteorological service to issue a second-level (orange) warning already on Wednesday for Bács-Kiskun, Csongrád-Csanád, Fejér, Győr-Moson-Sopron, Komárom-Esztergom, Pest, Tolna, Vas, and Veszprém counties. Forecasts indicate that the heat will intensify on Friday: in Komárom-Esztergom, Fejér, Pest, and Bács-Kiskun counties the mean temperature will exceed 29 degrees, while in Borsod-Abaúj-Zemplén and Szabolcs-Szatmár-Bereg counties it will exceed 25 degrees, and elsewhere it will exceed 27 degrees.
The minister for family and social affairs announced on Thursday that the nationwide package of measures known as the red code will come into effect again due to the heat alert.
Vilmos Kátai-Németh wrote that prolonged heatwaves — especially temperatures above 40 degrees — place the greatest strain on the bodies of children, the elderly, people with disabilities, and those with chronic illnesses, while homeless people face even greater danger due to the extreme heat. He therefore called on everyone to pay heightened attention to those living in their immediate surroundings.
The spokesperson for the National Directorate General for Water Management told MTI that not a drop of rain is expected in the coming days at Lake Velence and its catchment area. Gabriella Siklós said the current water level stands at 33 centimetres, the lowest value recorded since measurements began. In this situation, the Fejér County Government Office has imposed a bathing ban at five beaches on Lake Velence from 23 July due to bacterial contamination, and swimming is prohibited at the affected beaches until water quality is restored.
Budapest’s service providers and institutions have prepared for the prolonged heat, Mayor Gergely Karácsony announced on his Facebook page. He added that despite the record-low water level on the Danube, Budapest Waterworks continues to be able to supply Budapest with drinking water, meaning no water restrictions are necessary.
He also reported that Budapest Public Utilities will immediately begin cooling tram rails with water if that becomes necessary, and that in the event of a third-degree heat alert, asphalting works will be scheduled for night-time hours. The Mayor also announced that drinking fountains at the busiest railway stations will be available to assist travellers.
Drinking water suppliers are calling on residents to use water sparingly and responsibly due to the expected extreme heat. Észak-magyarországi Regionális Vízművek Zrt. has asked people on its website to use water economically and to avoid filling swimming pools or washing cars, in order to ensure the continuous provision of drinking water services. Commercial consumers were asked to schedule high-volume usage outside peak hours.
The company stated that its water supply systems are operating normally, and that the technical and staffing conditions are in place to meet the increased demand for water.
Duna Menti Regionális Vízmű Zrt. also drew attention to the need for economical drinking water use. It noted that the exceptionally low water level of the Danube has fallen below the lowest value ever recorded, and that in the coming days a further drop in water levels is expected, which in turn is likely to reduce drinking water production capacity in its operational area.
The company indicated that if drinking water consumption does not decrease noticeably, it will once again be forced to initiate the imposition of water restrictions. The water management sector has prepared to ensure the cooling water supply of the Paks nuclear power plant. László Gajdos, the minister responsible for the living environment, stated that experts are on standby to ensure the cooling water supply of the Paks nuclear power plant even in the face of the Danube’s extremely low water levels.
According to the statement, after the declaration of a state of extraordinary emergency, the water management authority immediately began the necessary interventions: four pump pontoons and two floating cranes were placed on standby on the Danube section near Paks. Although pumping is not yet necessary, 55 specialists are working on site in round-the-clock standby to ensure that the cooling water supply remains completely safe despite the extremely low water levels, he added.
“The protection effort is continuous — we are watching over the country’s water reserves and safety!” the politician concluded his post.
Additional drinking fountains have been installed for the duration of the third-level heat alert, and mist gates are operating across the country due to the extreme heat. In Szeged, on Klauzál Square, Szegedi Vízmű Zrt. is operating a mist gate, and alongside the existing ones, an additional drinking fountain has been installed on the square in front of the Móra Ferenc Museum.
The Szentes municipal government has designated cooling points in six public institutions for the duration of the third-level heat alert, and during the heat alert mist gates are operating on Kossuth Square and in Millennium Park.
In Pécs, the municipal government is providing nearly fifty drinking water access points at various locations around the city, while the city operations company has already erected sun sails to shade the pedestrian streets in the inner city; watering vehicles will operate along more than fifty kilometres of routes, and the mist gates of the city’s water supplier, Tettye Forrásház Zrt., are operating at six locations.
